newsitem.title: UK: Metals market players smarting from zinc losses.
newsitem.headline: Metals market players smarting from zinc losses.

text.p: Metals market players are nursing wounds from last week's plunge in zinc, suffering losses that likely run into the millions of dollars, traders and analysts said.
But profits from bull runs in zinc and other metals so far this year should offset much of the red ink, they added.
Three month zinc prices on the London Metal Exchange dived $300, or 20 percent, in the space of an hour last Tuesday from a seven-year peak of $1,675.
"Everybody was hurt on this move, very few people make money on big drops," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
"There are a lot of nightmare stories around," said an LME floor trader.

One trader was said to have just stepped out for a haircut when prices dropped. Traders added that a brokerage was heard to have lost a month's profit in a few hours and also that the biggest hit had been taken by a U.S. investment bank.
Once prices started to collapse, they tumbled in $20 increments as buyers disappeared.

"The overall move may not have been as big as Sumitomo, but the speed was much faster," one options trader said, referring to the plunge in copper prices last year after Sumitomo uncovered a web of unauthorised trades that led to $2.6 billion in losses.
Unwinding of option hedges accelerated the fall, traders said.
"Everybody was trying to sell, it was not easy to stem the flow, it just haemorrhaged," analyst Helen Williamson of brokers Brandeis said, adding that LME ring dealers were in a fix.
"LME brokers have to make a market whatever happens and they are obliged to take a minimum of five lots," she added.
Most traders and analysts said total losses probably ran into the millions of dollars but good profits from zinc's bull market and other markets should ease the pain.
Most houses have locked in good gains from zinc, which is still up nearly 50 percent since starting the year around $1,050, basis three months.
"For the LME brokers it's a wound, but one that will heal," a floor trader said.
Squires said: "You always hear about the bad times, but zinc has been a potentially very profitable market this year."
